govwin role guide · Customer Admin

Build a Winning Proposal, End-to-End

The complete customer manual: every feature of your proposal portal, in the order you use it — rank opportunities, build a content library, draft a proposal from your atoms in the canvas, lock the matrix, and export submission-ready files.

Every step was verified on a real effort: the Immobileyes NAVAIR/NAVSEA Counter-UAS SBIR (topic DON26BX03-NP002). The screenshots are that live run.

Complete surface · every feature, screen, and control — verified on a live build

Your portal — orientation

where /portal/<company>/dashboard

Welcome to your company’s proposal portal. This guide walks every feature you have as a Customer Admin, in the order you use them — from a ranked opportunity to a submission-ready, downloadable proposal. Sign in with the credentials your RFP-Pipeline admin issued; you land on your Dashboard.

The sidebar & global chrome

The left sidebar is your map. It shows your company name, a notification bell, and your name up top; every workspace below.

The notification bell polls every 60s and badges unread (or 9+). If an RFP admin is working inside your company on your behalf, an amber shadow-admin banner shows at the top — everything they do is logged to your audit trail.

The Dashboard — home base

where /portal/<company>/dashboard

Your dashboard is role-aware: quick stats, your ToDo queue, an Add content dropzone, a getting-started checklist, and recent activity.

A trial banner appears if your trial is ending — it turns red within 7 days and links to Billing so you keep your data.

  1. Check the three stat cards (Library Units · Active Proposals · Pinned Topics) — each links to its screen.
  2. Work Your To-Dos. Each card shows an urgency chip, a workflow pill, a step trail, and a typed action (Acknowledge / Approve-Done / Open-to-upload / a form).
  3. Drop a file on Add content to upload & atomize it straight into your library.
  4. Tick off the Get Started checklist (upload docs · set up profile · create a bucket · purchase a portal).

Opportunities — your ranked pipeline

where /portal/<company>/cards

The Opportunity Pipeline is every opportunity the platform has released to you, ranked by your Spotlight buckets. Pin one to pull its documents into your workspace, then purchase a build.

  1. Toggle Include closed to widen the list; Refresh re-pulls; the count shows how many cards you have.
  2. Read a card: title, a submission-stage badge (NOFO / Pre-Release / Updated / Closed / Archived), agency, program type, and the close date.
  3. Pin (copy docs) copies the solicitation’s documents into your workspace; a pinned card then shows Unpin and a green Purchase. Build → opens the build page. An Update available strip offers Resync when the RFP changes.

Purchasing a proposal workspace

The green Purchase button opens the purchase modal.

In the verified run, the NAVAIR/NAVSEA C-UAS topic DON26BX03-NP002 ranked #1 for Immobileyes — the best fit for a counter-drone optics company.

  1. The offer is a one-time expert-curated proposal build. Pay by card runs Stripe checkout, or use an Access / discount code.
  2. Enter your comp code (e.g. rfppipelinetest) and Complete purchase. The build opens in curation_pending — an RFP admin then releases it (72h SLA), provisioning your matrix and molds.

Buckets — your scoring lenses

where /portal/<company>/buckets

Spotlight buckets are your scoring criteria — the themes you care about. Each bucket ranks the whole pipeline by your rules, and editing one re-ranks your Opportunities automatically.

  1. In New bucket, set a Name plus any of keywords, agencies, program types, and NAICS codes; tick Include closed opportunities if you want them scored. Click Create.
  2. Click Rank → on a bucket to see your pipeline ordered #1, #2, … with each opportunity’s score and per-factor chips (e.g. keyword 3).
  3. Delete a bucket with its ✕. Ranking is deterministic today; an optional scoring agent overlays it later.

Library — build your content atoms

where /portal/<company>/atoms

Your library is the raw material every draft is built from. You deconstruct your documents into tagged, sized atoms, then compose and reuse them. The page has three tabs — Library, Upload package, Atomize — plus a reuse-a-past-proposal panel.

Browse, filter & compose

  1. Filter with the search box, the grain select (primitive / group / foundational), the status select, and a My atoms / All atoms toggle. Click a tag chip to filter by it.
  2. Select atoms with their checkboxes to reveal the bulk bar: Approve all, Archive all, and a tag-dimension + value → Tag all.
  3. With two or more selected, name the group (e.g. “Team for Navy”) and Group into new atom to compose a reusable bundle.
  4. Click an atom title to open its detail drawer — confirmed vs unconfirmed tags, lineage (↖ derived from / ↳ reused in), and a content preview.
Atom vocabulary
FacetValues
Grainprimitive (one block) · group (a bundle) · foundational (a whole reference doc)
Sourceuploaded · returned (harvested back from a locked section)
Visibilityprivate · admin-only · shared
Statusdraft · approved · archived

Upload a package (bulk atomize)

The fastest way to fill the library: drop a whole proposal package and let the atomizer shred it.

Verified: five Immobileyes documents atomized into 24 atoms — tagged vol:technical vol:cost vol:key_personnel kind:bio and more.

  1. On Upload package, drop up to 12 files (PDF·DOCX·PPTX·XLSX·TXT·MD) or Choose files.
  2. Add optional Package context (name, agency, program, phase, solicitation, topic) — it’s stamped on every atom minted from the package.
  3. Click Atomize package. Each file becomes a reference atom plus one primitive per substantive block, auto-tagged against the taxonomy.

Atomize — the hand-shredder

The Atomize tab is precision control: paste or upload a document, and box exactly what becomes an atom.

  1. Paste text (a bio, a past-performance blurb, a whole team section) and Deconstruct, or upload a file. The document becomes a list of typed objects (figure / table / list / heading / text).
  2. Set the Session context (the “FROM” pedigree — agency, program, phase, solicitation, topic) so everything minted this session inherits it.
  3. Select an object, give it a title, add curated + free tags, and Make atom (or Make group for a table/list). Minted atoms collect in the Section tray.
  4. Select several tray items, name it, and Box section to wrap them into a section group.

Reuse a past proposal (templify)

At the top of the page, Reuse a past proposal lists your uploaded proposals. Save as template extracts a proposal’s structure into a reusable skeleton (pick a template type → Extract structure); once templated, New draft spins up a fresh document from that skeleton. This is how a winning structure becomes the starting point for the next bid.

Proposals — your builds

where /portal/<company>/proposals

Every proposal for your company. Proposals aren’t created here — they appear when you purchase a topic and an RFP admin releases it.

  1. Each row shows the title, agency, topic, section count, created date, a due/closed date (red if overdue), and a stage pill in the customer V0.5 → V1 labels.
  2. Click a row to open its build workspace (the compliance matrix).
Proposal stages (what the pill means)
PillMeaning
V0.5 · Draftbuilding — sections being drafted
V0.5 · Reviewin internal review
V1 · Finallocked & ready to submit
V1 · Submittedsubmitted to the agency
Archivedclosed out

The proposal workspace & compliance matrix

where /portal/<company>/proposals/<id>

Opening a proposal gives you the build cockpit: a stage-control bar, the volume/section matrix, team & access, compliance, AI, and export. As an admin you get the full admin panel (four tabs).

The stage-control bar

After two proposal locks, further changes require RFP-Pipeline support — the bar says so. Downloads unlock once the proposal is locked/submitted.

  1. The bar shows stage progress dots for each gate (done ✓ / current / future), the due date, and a gate-requirements button (N requirement(s) pending or All gates met ✓).
  2. The primary action is Advance to {next} →; at Final you get Unlock for Edit / Re-lock. If an advance is blocked, an amber list names the unlocked sections (admins can Force advance anyway →).

The admin panel — 4 tabs

The admin panel is your build console.

  1. In Artifacts, each section row shows a status pill, assignee, a page-fill bar, and Accept & Lock (→ 🔒 Unlock). When every section in a volume is locked, the volume reads ✓ Volume locked and the Download + PDF links light up.
  2. The export row — Download Proposal (.docx) and Download all (.zip) — enables once the proposal is locked.
Admin-panel tabs
TabWhat you do
Artifactsvolume groups with per-section Accept & Lock, page-fill gauges, Lock Volume, Download (docx) / PDF, Accept & Lock All, and the whole-proposal export row
Team & Accessthe TeamManager — invite collaborators, per-section grants, the E/C/V access matrix
ComplianceRun Compliance Check (AI), the compliance checklist, and stage-gate requirements
AI & LibraryDraft with AI across empty sections, and Record Outcome (Won/Lost/Withdrawn)

Compliance, team & AI tabs

The other three admin-panel tabs run your review, your people, and your AI.

Invite grants are per section and per permission (view / comment / edit). A collaborator only ever sees the sections you assign — see the Collaborator guide for the full picture.

  1. Compliance tab — Run Compliance Check fires an AI pass that scores your proposal against the solicitation’s requirements (pass/fail/partial per variable). Below it, the Compliance Checklist and the Stage Gate Requirements (add a gate with a stage + label, toggle each met).
  2. Team & Access tab — the TeamManager: + Invite a collaborator (email, name, role, permission, and the sections to assign), then read the Access Matrix (sections × people, E/C/V cells).
  3. AI & Library tab — Draft with AI queues a draft for every empty section; Record Outcome (Won/Lost/Withdrawn, once submitted) feeds the result back into your library so winning content ranks higher next time.

Opportunity origin & compliance

The collapsible Opportunity origin & compliance card has three tabs — Overview (build stage, lock count, deadlines), Origin (frozen-at-purchase: opportunity, agency, program, topic #, solicitation #, bought-from bucket), and Compliance (a live “{x}/{y} mandatory satisfied — {pct}%” bar and a Satisfied / Partial / Not-addressed / N-A grid). It’s your at-a-glance readiness read.

The section canvas — where you write

where /portal/<company>/proposals/<id>/sections/<sectionId>

The canvas is the WYSIWYG editor for one section — what you see is what exports. Open a section from the matrix. The top bar carries the title, a status pill, export buttons, Undo/Redo, + From Library, Save, and (admins) Complete & Lock.

The formatting toolbar & node types

  1. The INSERT group adds a block after the selected one; the FORMAT group (B / I / align / size / color) acts on the selected text block.
  2. Click any node to edit it in place; drag the handle to reorder. Each node type has its own inline editor.
Canvas node types
NodeInline editing
Headinglevel (H1/H2/H3), numbering, text
Text blocktextarea + B / I / U / superscript / subscript mini-toolbar
Bulleted / Numbered listper-item text, indent/outdent, add/remove item
Imageclick-to-upload, alt text, caption, size, replace
Tableeditable headers/cells, + Row / + Column, delete
Captionprefix (Figure/Table/Chart), number, text
Footnote / URLmarker + text / href + display text
TOCauto-lists the document’s headings
Page break / Spacerstructural

The toolbox sidebar

The sidebar opens on Your toolbox — a prioritized card list resolved from your role and the stage — then offers tabs.

Sidebar tabs
TabPurpose
Compliancedocument status, a real word-budget gauge (“{words}/{max} words · N-page limit”), fonts/margins, content-source dots (AI / library / manual)
Node / Selectthe selected block’s provenance + actions (Move, Accept, Revert, Delete, Replace from Library), a full Format panel, per-node History, Comments, and an AI Revision panel
Adda 12-button grid of every node type
Review“Review · Modify · Lock” — admins get Complete & Lock this section; others save for an admin to lock
Historythe version list (AI Draft / Human Edit / Library / …) — click any to preview
Settingsthe floorplan — margins, fonts, line spacing, page/slide limit, header/footer templates

Draft & revise with AI

Verified: the proposal.draft_section agent ran on all 8 Technical-Volume sections, grounded in the atomized library, to a ~1,090-word / 2-page target per section. Nothing auto-commits — it’s advisory until you accept.

  1. Click Draft (or Draft all sections from the admin panel). The drafting agent reads the RFP context and the section’s mold, pulls the most relevant atoms, and writes canvas content sized to the page budget.
  2. On a text node, open AI Revision for one-click rewrites: Regenerate · Make shorter · Make longer · More specific · Simpler language · Stronger opening · Add metrics · Fix compliance, or a custom instruction.

Insert & replace from the library

  1. + From Library opens the insert panel: it ranks your atoms for this section (with “✦ N context match(es)”). Tick atoms and Insert N atom(s) into the canvas — they become section nodes.
  2. The picked atoms flow straight into the canvas as editable nodes.
  3. On a selected node, Replace from Library swaps its content for a better-matching atom (sortable by best-match / most-used / most-recent).
  4. Drag nodes to reorder them into the flow you want.

Harvest back to the library

The Library (N) button opens the atomize rail — each library-eligible node becomes a bubble you can classify (choose a type), tag, and Accept as atom, harvesting your best content back into the library for reuse. Accept all does the batch.

Accept & Lock

Verified: locking turned 10 matrix rows green (8 Technical + 2 Cost); Volume 2 read “8/8 locked · 9/10 pages · ✓ Volume locked.”

  1. When a section is right, Complete & Lock (top bar or the Review tab). Locking flips its compliance row to satisfied, snapshots the version, and harvests reusable content back to your library.
  2. Locked sections are read-only; Unlock reopens one for edits (admins).

The slide editor

When the artifact is a slide deck, the same shell becomes the SlideEditor.

  1. The left Slides panel is your thumbnail navigator — each thumb shows the slide title and element count; + Add Slide appends one (you can’t delete the last).
  2. Edit the active slide with the embedded canvas (16:9 or 4:3). The info bar reads “Slide N of M · N element(s).” Export the deck with Export .pptx from the top bar.

The spreadsheet editor

A spreadsheet artifact (like a Cost Volume) opens the SheetEditor — a real grid with formulas.

Verified: the Cost Volume exported to a submission-ready .xlsx with live formulas — Base $199,502 ≤ $200k, Option $114,464 ≤ $115k.

  1. Use the cell-reference box (e.g. A1) and the formula bar (fx) to enter values and formulas; the format bar handles bold, alignment, fill color, size, and font.
  2. Add rows/columns with the trailing + controls; manage multiple sheet tabs at the bottom (double-click to rename). Export .xlsx writes the workbook with formulas intact.

Compliance Review — the readiness check

where /portal/<company>/proposals/<id>/review

A read-only readiness view across sections and the compliance matrix.

The top banner reads Ready for Final Submission (green) or Not Ready — Items Need Attention (amber), with a stats bar (Sections Locked · Requirements Met · Est. Pages · Stage). Below, a Section Status table (with page estimates and “(over)” flags) and a Compliance Checklist (each requirement’s status, source, and notes). Use it as your pre-submit gate.

Documents — everything in one place

where /portal/<company>/documents

Every document across the workspace, in five tables: your standalone documents, proposal sections, supporting documents, library uploads, and solicitation source documents.

  1. + New Document starts a standalone canvas document; Upload Document sends a file to the library.
  2. In Supporting Documents, use the per-row actions: Upload (presigned), Download, and admin Review / Approve / Waive to advance a required attachment’s status.

New document chooser

Start blank offers four presets — One-page flier, Blank document, Slide deck, Workbook. Start from a template filters your templates and the system library; each card previews the structure and Use template opens the editor. A standalone document has its own Lock for download bar.

Activity & Processes — audit and automation

where /portal/<company>/activity · /processes

Two monitoring surfaces.

Activity is your audit timeline — namespace tabs (All/Proposal/Library/…), a type search, time ranges, auto-refresh, and expandable event payloads. Processes lists your running automations with health chips (Failing/Stalled/Awaiting input/Running/Done); admins can Move to next gate on a paused step and expand the Steps timeline.

Team — members & collaborators

where /portal/<company>/team

Manage who’s in your workspace.

  1. Invite a member with Email, Name, and Role (Contributor / Admin / External Partner).
  2. The Team Members table lets admins Deactivate / Reactivate a member (never hard-deleted). Proposal Collaborators lists per-proposal partners and their accepted/pending status.

Automation, Settings & Billing

where /automation · /profile · /billing · /portals · /agents

Your account and preferences.

Automation preferences

Automation (admins) toggles notifications (document ready · collaborator get-ready · stage advanced · new priority opportunity), AI (review on advance), and flow (auto-advance when all locked). Save to apply.

Company profile

Settings shows your account + subscription and the editable Company Profile (legal name, website, summary, technology focus, NAICS, set-asides, target agencies, keywords). These fields feed proposal templates and AI drafting, so keep them current.

Billing & Builds & AI Usage

Billing manages your Spotlight subscription, expert-consulting hours, and purchase history. Builds (/portals) lists your purchased proposal portals with their lifecycle status (curation_pending shows the 72h SLA countdown; launched/executing offer stage controls). AI Usage (/agents) shows your agent calls, allocation used, per-agent breakdown, and recent activity.

Export — your submission-ready files

where Download Proposal (.docx) · Cost Volume (.xlsx)

With a volume locked, download your deliverables. The Technical Volume exports to a submission-ready .docx (US-Letter, 1″ margins, the agency’s fonts, figures inline & captioned); the Cost Volume to an .xlsx with live formulas.

Verified deliverables: a 10-page Technical Volume .docx (6 figures, 5 tables, 8 DON TV2 sections) and a Cost Volume .xlsx — Base $199,502 ≤ $200k, Option $114,464 ≤ $115k, formulas live.
